paper_metadata.title: Practical Meta-Reinforcement Learning of Evolutionary Strategy with Quantum Neural Networks for Stock Trading

summary: The paper studies meta-learning for stock trading with classical MAML/CAVIA and quantum continuous-variable neural networks Q-MAML/Q-CAVIA. On the reported back-test, the classical baselines achieved 0.76% ROI (MAML) and 0.16% ROI (CAVIA) versus a market-value baseline of 0.86%, while the quantum models performed worse, with ROIs of -27.70%, -28.93%, -36.85%, and -30.41% depending on beamsplitter use.

experiments.description: Quantum meta-learning stock-trading experiment using a continuous-variable quantum neural network for Q-MAML, evaluated with and without a beamsplitter gate on a simulated quantum computer.

algorithm.variant: Q-MAML with continuous-variable quantum neural network; compared with and without beamsplitter gate
algorithm.ansatz: Continuous-variable quantum neural network with layers of displacement, rotation, squeezing, Kerr, and optionally beamsplitter gates
algorithm.convergence_criteria: trained for 25 epochs on the meta-training portfolios and 5 epochs on the test portfolio in the quantum setting
algorithm.parameter_initialization: not_specified; context parameters initialized to 0 for CAVIA, but Q-MAML parameter initialization not explicitly stated

problem_formulation.encoding_details: closing prices are encoded into each wire via a displacement gate; one wire per stock plus one cash-bias wire
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize portfolio value / return on investment via learned portfolio weights over time
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: softmax output enforces portfolio weights sum to 1

problem_instance.description: Stock portfolio trading on Consumer Cyclical stocks using meta-learning on unseen portfolios
problem_instance.dataset_name: Yahoo Finance Consumer Cyclical stock data

dataset_specification.preprocessing: closing prices only; 70/30 train-test split; window size 10; prices restricted to $0-$50; logarithmic rate of return normalization

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Use only closing prices; group past 10 days as input; normalize with logarithmic rate of return; train/test split 70/30; backtest on held-out period
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 8 independent runs; report mean ROI and standard deviation; compare against market value baseline

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: portfolio construction from Yahoo Finance data; windowing; normalization; softmax portfolio-weight output
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: ROI calculation and comparison to market value baseline

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: training reward increases over epochs; beamsplitter variants perform better

speedup_claims.conditions: Backtest on ABC and AKAM over 7/2/2001 to 9/21/2001 using simulated continuous-variable quantum neural networks
speedup_claims.caveats: No quantum model outperformed the market value baseline; beamsplitter variants performed better than non-beamsplitter variants, but still underperformed buy and hold.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: A real quantum computer with substantially more qumodes/wires, more training epochs, and a larger portfolio size than 2 stocks would be needed; the paper only demonstrates a simulated CV quantum neural network.
limiting_factors: No demonstrated quantum advantage over the classical baseline
Simulation on a classical computer rather than quantum hardware
Classical MAML baseline outperforms Q-MAML on the reported ROI comparison

notes: hardware.type reported as a simulated continuous-variable quantum machine using PennyLane on a classical computer

num_qubits inferred from the paper's statement that Q-MAML used 3 wires for 2 stocks plus 1 cash wire, while the broader quantum setup mentions up to 5 qumodes; the experiment compares Q-MAML and Q-CAVIA but Q-MAML specifically uses 3 wires
circuit_depth reported as 4 layers of gates
speedup_order inferred because the paper discusses practical performance but does not provide asymptotic quantum/classical complexity or a proven speedup

experiments.description: Classical meta-learning baseline experiment for MAML stock trading on Consumer Cyclical stocks using NES optimization.

algorithm.variant: MAML with NES optimizer for stock trading
algorithm.ansatz: Classical neural network with 2 hidden layers

key_results: Trained for 2500 epochs on 5 portfolios of 5 stocks each, then meta-tested for 20 epochs on the unseen portfolio.
Back-test on ABC, AKAM, APD, AVP, BAC from 2002-01-07 to 2002-06-12 gave $10,075.89 end amount and 0.76% ROI.
Market value baseline was $10,085.50 and 0.86% ROI.
